opening.text: There was a boy called Ade, 15, who spent every Saturday helping at a busy bike repair workshop.
Riders wheeled in bikes with flat tyres, and Ade patched tube after tube.
A rider came in after walking 8 kilometres home, all because of one tiny thorn. "Why can't a tyre just fix itself?" Ade wondered.

card.goal: Make a balloon or tube that seals itself after a pin prick
card.rules: The fix must happen by itself, with no hands. An adult does the pricking.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Riders keep getting stranded by punctures at Ade's workshop. Can you help him build a tyre that heals itself? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a hunch about self-repair. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature fixes its own wounds every day. Tap each card to meet four self-healers!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Predict first: which liquid will drip the least? Keep everything else the same, and hold every cup over the tray.
guide.sketch: Draw your balloon before and after the prick, like a materials engineer!
guide.build_and_test: An adult pricks, you time. How many minutes does your balloon stay up?
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Use your friend's feedback, change ONE thing, and test again.
guide.ending: And ever since then, Ade's workshop has kept a jar of self-healing sealant on the shelf, and riders get home, even after a thorn.

quick_check.question: One tyre needs about 60 ml of sealant. How much does Ade need for 3 bikes with 2 tyres each?
quick_check.right: Right! 3 bikes × 2 tyres = 6 tyres, and 6 × 60 = 360 ml.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. First count the tyres: 3 bikes × 2 tyres each.

clue_cards.name: Rubber tree
clue_cards.trick: Milky latex flows into a cut.
clue_cards.does: In the air, it clumps into a rubbery plug.

clue_cards.name: Skin
clue_cards.does: They clump and mesh to plug a small cut in minutes.

clue_cards.name: Mussel
clue_cards.trick: Threads with bonds that break and join again.
clue_cards.does: A stretched thread heals itself, even underwater.

clue_cards.name: Pine tree
clue_cards.trick: Sticky resin oozes over a wound.
clue_cards.does: It hardens in air into a seal against insects.

predict.prompt: Seals itself or stays broken? Predict first!

items.label: A cut in a pine tree's bark
A plain balloon pricked by a pin
A tubeless tyre with sealant, hit by a thorn

predict.explain: Self-healing needs a repair kit on the inside and a push to move it into the hole. A plain balloon has neither, so its stretched rubber just tears.

lab.title: The leaky cup lab
lab.predict: Each cup has one pin hole. Which liquid will drip the least in 1 minute?

tool.name: I Like, I Wish, What If
tool.intro: I Like, I Wish, What If is how designers give kind, useful feedback on a prototype. Ask a friend, or be your own critic, and start every comment with one of three phrases. Today you'll use all 3.

parts.name: I like…
parts.what: Say what works, and be specific.
parts.example: 🍶 I like that the lid clicks shut, so it never leaks in my bag.

parts.name: I wish…
parts.what: Say kindly what could be better.
parts.example: 🍶 I wish it fitted in my bike's bottle holder.

parts.name: What if…?
parts.example: 🍶 What if the lid had a strap, so I could clip it on?

sketch_checklist: I drew my balloon before and after the prick, as cross-sections.
I showed where the sealant sits and how air pressure pushes it into the hole.
I labelled what jams the hole and what makes it harden.

test.measure: minutes the balloon stays up after a prick
test.check_question: Fair test check: how many times did you repeat each balloon test?

reflection.question: Which nature trick did your sealant copy?
